ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$, $AC=8$, $AB=10$. Let $D$ and $E$ be the midpoints of $AC$ and $AB$ respectively. Connect $DE$. What is the length of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\triangle ABC$, $BC=\sqrt{AB^{2}-AC^{2}}=\sqrt{10^{2}-8^{2}}=6$, \\
since D and E are the midpoints of AC and AB respectively, \\
therefore $DE=\frac{1}{2}BC=\frac{1}{2}\times 6=\boxed{3}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle ABC, with a right-angle mark at point C; AC is the left vertical side, and BC is the bottom horizontal side, so AC and BC are two mutually perpendicular legs, and AB is the hypotenuse. Point D is located on AC, point E is located on AB, and segment DE connects D and E, and appears to be parallel to BC. Reasoning: The problem gives angle ACB = 90°, AC = 8, AB = 10, and D and E are respectively the midpoints of AC and AB. Since AB is the hypotenuse of the right triangle, by the Pythagorean theorem, BC = sqrt(AB^2 - AC^2) = sqrt(10^2 - 8^2) = sqrt(100 - 64) = sqrt(36) = 6. D and E are respectively the midpoints of the two sides AC and AB in triangle ABC, so DE is the midline of the triangle, DE = BC/2 = 6/2 = 3.
